title: fastpath-cache-miss-heuristic-causing-per-key-throttle-inconsistency
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Some requests intermittently bypass per-key/per-route throttles when the fastpath admission heuristic observes a cache miss for token metadata and falls back to a permissive global allowance. The symptom is bursty, client-specific overages (short windows of token unthrottled traffic) that do not align with per-key rate policies. This has been observed after policy updates and during policy rollout windows where metadata TTLs are being refreshed.
repro_steps: 1) Create a token with a custom per-key burst policy (small per-second window + monthly quota).
2) Deploy a policy change (increase burst credit) and trigger policy propagation for the org, causing metadata version bump.
3) Send concurrent requests from the token at high QPS while the metadata cache TTLs are expiring on several edge nodes.
4) Observe that some requests take the fastpath evaluation and attribute to the global fallback bucket instead of the token-local bucket, resulting in short-lived unthrottled bursts.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial alert from billing detector (unusual per-token token-rate variance) and customer report describing short bursts of allowed requests despite apparent quota hits.
2026-03-11: Correlated with policy-change events and fastpath admission metric spikes on edge nodes in us-west-2.

2026-03-12: Added additional logging to fastpath path to record metadata_cache_state, metadata_version_seen, and admission_decision_reason. Logs show decisions labeled 'fastpath-cache-heuristic-fallback' during cache misses.

2026-03-13: Reproduced in staging with controlled TTLs: when metadata cache returns empty and heuristic was triggered, code used a permissive fallback that checked only global route-level buckets, not per-key buckets.
observability_signals: policy-propagation.latency (some nodes showed >15s lag during rollout)
per-route-metering-discrepancy (sampled requests show global bucket attribution instead of per-key)
root_cause: Race between the fastpath admission heuristic and async metadata propagation. On cache miss, the heuristic opted for a permissive global fallback path that did not consult authoritative per-key policy state. When policy updates and TTL refreshes were happening concurrently, some edge nodes made decisions based on stale or empty metadata thus failing to enforce per-key quotas for a short window.
mitigation: Short term: force-disable the fastpath cache-miss heuristic for all keys with recent policy changes (flagged via policy_version > X) and reduce metadata TTL to 1s for high-volume namespaces. Also added an emergency circuit that routes cache-miss decisions to synchronous metadata lookup for top-500 orgs.
proposed_fix: Change fastpath admission to never assume a permissive global fallback on metadata cache miss. Instead: 1) perform a synchronous authoritative metadata read when a cache miss occurs for keys with non-default policies; 2) for keys with default policies allow current fastpath; 3) add a signing/version check to metadata so edge nodes can detect 'stale vs unknown' and trigger a safe deny-or-defer policy. Update the cache invalidation path to broadcast policy version bumps immediately to active shards.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fastpath decision matrix covering: cache-hit/valid, cache-hit/stale-version, cache-miss-sync-lookup, cache-miss-permissive-fallback (deprecated).
Integration test in staging that runs policy-change + high-QPS replay and asserts no global-bucket attributions for per-key-limited tokens.
Chaos test: kill metadata sync worker and ensure admission path safely denies/deferred instead of permissive allow.
Add a targeted shadowing run in production for 48 hours where authoritative decisions are logged and compared to fastpath decisions for sampling.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge fix to canary runtime in us-west-2 with shadow logging (PRs linked below).
2) Monitor per-token burst anomalies and fastpath.fallback_count for 24h; revert if we observe regressed latency > 5ms on p95 fastpath path.
3) Expand canary to all regions over 48h with staged config rollout (start with reserved/dedicated customers).
4) Full rollout when shadow mismatch rate <0.01% for 72h and no SLO regressions.
follow_ups: Post-mortem to include timeline, customer-impact table, and billing reconciliation plan.
Add synthetic policy-change + load test to CI to prevent regressions.
Consider a stronger guarantee: policy change must block for outstanding fastpath windows for X seconds or until distributed version ack is received for critical orgs.
Billing team to run reconciliation for tokens flagged in the anomaly window and issue credits where necessary.
